Surah Al-Buruj (The Constellations)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the sky containing the constellations﴾. These are the twelve constellations (buruj). It is also said: the stars, or the great luminous bodies.
﴿By the Promised Day﴾, the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And by the witness and the witnessed﴾. That is: a witness on that Day, and a witnessed Day. By "the witness" is meant everyone among the creatures who bears witness on it, and by "the witnessed" is meant the wonders that occur on that Day. The indefiniteness of the two nouns may be explained either by what I mentioned in His saying, "a soul will know what it has presented," as if it were said: "what its abundance has exceeded of a witness and a witnessed," or by the vagueness of the description, as if it were said: "and a witness and a witnessed whose description cannot be fully grasped." The commentators have offered many views about the two. It is said: Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Day of Resurrection; or Jesus, peace be upon him, and his community, based on His saying, ﴿And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 117]; or the community of Muhammad and all the other nations; or the Black Stone and the pilgrims; or the days and the nights; or the children of Adam, based on the hadith: "Every day calls out: 'I am a new day, and I am a witness over what is done in me, so make use of me, for if my sun sets, it will not reach me until the Day of Resurrection.'" Or it is the recording angels and the children of Adam; or Allah (Exalted) and the creation, based on His saying (Exalted): ﴿And Allah suffices as a witness﴾ [al-Nisa': 166]; or the prophets and Muhammad (ﷺ) [peace be upon them]. The answer to the oath is omitted, and it is indicated by what follows:

"Destroyed were the companions of the trench" (qutila ashab al-ukhdud). That is, cursed (luʿina). It is as if it were said: "I swear by these things that they are cursed," meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh, just as the companions of the trench were cursed. Ukhdud is the plural of khadd, that is, a great cleft in the earth.

It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ): "There was a sorcerer for one of the kings. When he grew old, he attached to himself a boy to teach him sorcery. On the boy's route there was a monk, and he listened to him. One day on his way he saw an animal that had blocked the people, so he took a stone and said: 'O Allah, if the monk is dearer to You than the sorcerer, then kill it.' So he killed it. After that the boy would heal the blind and the leper. A companion of the king had gone blind, and he healed him. The king saw him and asked him: 'Who restored your sight to you?' He said: 'My Lord.' The king became angry and tortured him, and he pointed to the boy. The boy was tortured, and he pointed to the monk. The monk did not turn back from his religion, so he was sawn in two with a saw. The boy refused, so he was taken to a mountain to be thrown from its peak. He supplicated, and the mountain shook with the people, so they fell, and he was saved. He was taken to a boat, and they pressed him to drown him, but he supplicated, and the boat capsized with them, and they drowned, and he was saved. He said to the king: 'You will not kill me until you gather the people in an open ground, crucify me on a trunk, take an arrow from my quiver, and say: "In the name of Allah, Lord of the boy," then shoot me with it.' He shot him, and it struck his temple, so he placed his hand upon it and died. The people said: 'We believe in the Lord of the boy.' It was said to the king: 'What you were fearing has come upon you.' So he dug a trench, filled it with fire, and whoever did not turn back from his religion he threw into it, until a woman came with a child, and she hesitated to fall into it. The child said: 'O mother, be patient, for you are upon the truth,' so the child and his mother were thrown into it."

ال﴿The Fire﴾ is a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimal) from "al-ukhdud" (the trench).

﴿Full of fuel﴾ is a description of it, meaning that it is a great fire, having in it what raises its flames: abundant firewood and human bodies.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 85, verse 6:

﴿Idh﴾ (when) is an adverbial complement (ẓarf) governing "qutila" (cursed be). That is: they were cursed when they burned them with fire, sitting around it. (p-624) ﴿Hum ʿalayha﴾ (they, sitting over it), that is, the disbelievers, upon what is near it from the edges of the trench.

﴿Quʿūd﴾ (sitting), meaning seated on chairs.

Translation:

﴿And they﴾, the disbelievers,

﴿over what they were doing to the believers﴾, of burning,

﴿are witnesses﴾, each of them bearing witness for the others before the King that none of them had neglected what he was commanded and entrusted with, of torture; and in this there is an exhortation to the believers to be patient and to endure the harm of the people of Makkah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 85, verse 8:

﴿And they did not find fault with them except that they believed﴾, and they did not criticize them, and they did not disapprove of anything except their faith, like his saying:

"There is no fault in them except that their swords..................."

And his saying:

"They found no fault with the Banu Umayyah except that they are forbearing when they are angry."

It is also read as "naqimu" with a kasra (naqimu), but the eloquent (fasih) form is with a fatha (naqamu).

﴿in God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾: He mentioned the attributes by which He deserves to be believed in, namely that He is Mighty (ʿAziz), Overpowering (Ghalib), Capable (Qadir), whose punishment is to be feared; Praiseworthy (Hamid), Bestowing blessings (Mun'im), for whose blessing praise is owed to Him, and whose reward is hoped for.

﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. Therefore everyone in them is bound to worship Him and to submit humbly to Him, as an affirmation of this, because what they held against them (the believers) is the truth, which none holds against except a falsifier (mubtil). And those who hold it against them deserve God's retribution against them with a great punishment.

﴿And God is witness over everything﴾. This is a threat to them, meaning: He knows what they did, and He will recompense them for it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 85, verse 10:

﴿Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women﴾. It is permissible that by "those who persecuted" is meant specifically the people of the trench (ashab al-ukhdud), and by "those who believed" are meant those thrown into the trench. The meaning of "fatanuhum" (they persecuted them) is that they tortured them with fire and burned them.

﴿Then they did not repent﴾, they did not turn back from their disbelief.

﴿Then for them﴾, in the Hereafter,

﴿is the punishment of Hell﴾, for their disbelief.

﴿And for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾, in this world, according to what is narrated: that the fire turned back upon them and burned them. It is also permissible that by "those who persecuted the believers" is meant in general those who tested them with harm, and "the believers" are those who were tested; and that the persecutors have two punishments in the Hereafter: one for their disbelief and one for their persecution.

Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds — for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph. (Qur'an 85:11)

That is, those who endured the torment of the trench (al-Ukhdud); or it is general.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿Indeed, the seizing of your Lord is severe.﴾

"Al-batsh" (the forceful seizing): taking with violence. When it is described as severe, it has been intensified and grown greatly. What is meant is His seizing of the oppressors and the tyrants, with punishment and retribution.

Verse: ﴿Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats.﴾ That is: He creates them initially, then He brings them back after He had turned them into dust. By His power over origination and repetition He indicates the severity of His seizing (of the wrongdoers). Or He threatens the disbelievers that He will bring them back as He originated them, so that He may seize them, since they did not give thanks for the blessing of origination and denied the return.

﴿And He is the Oft-Forgiving﴾, the Concealer of faults, the Pardoner of sins;

﴿the Most Loving﴾, the One who loves His friends (awliya'). It is also said: He is the One who does toward the people of His obedience what a loving one does, by giving them what they desire.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 85, verse 15:

﴿Dhu al-'Arsh (Lord of the Throne)﴾, its Creator and its Owner.

﴿al-Majid (the Glorious)﴾, read with a kasra (al-jarr) by Hamzah and 'Ali, on the basis that it is an attribute (sifah) of al-'Arsh (the Throne). The glory (majd) of Allah is His greatness ('azamah), and the glory of the Throne is its exaltedness ('uluww) and its greatness.

﴿فَعّالٌ﴾ (Doer of what He wills) is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada').

﴿لِما يُرِيدُ﴾ means "for what He wills," that is, His bringing it into existence (takwīnahu). So the verse indicates that God creates the actions of His servants.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 85, verse 17:

﴿Has there come to you the report of the hosts?﴾ The news of the armies that rebelled against God among the nations of old.

Pharaoh and Thamud. [Pharaoh and Thamud] is an apposition (badal) to "the hosts." By Pharaoh he means himself and his household (āluhu). The meaning is: you have come to know the denial of those hosts toward the Messengers, and what befell them because of their denial.

﴿Nay, but those who disbelieve﴾, from your people, ﴿are in denial﴾ and in seeking the punishment. They do not take warning from the hosts [of Pharaoh and Thamud], not because the state of the hosts was hidden from them, but they deny you out of obstinacy. [p. 626]

And Allah encompasses them from behind them. ﴿Allah encompasses them from behind them﴾: He is knowing of their circumstances, capable over them, and they cannot escape Him. The encompassing of them from behind them is a figurative expression (mathal), because they cannot elude Him, just as no one who flees can escape from a thing that encompasses him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 85, verse 21:

﴿Nay, it is﴾, nay, this which they denied,

﴿a glorious Qur'an﴾, noble, of high rank among the books, and in its composition and its inimitability; it is not as they claim, that it is fabricated, or that it is the fables of the ancients.

in a Preserved Tablet (lawh mahfuz), protected from the reach of the devils. "Mahfuz" (preserved) is an epithet (ṣifah) of the Qur'an, meaning: protected from alteration and change. The lawh, according to al-Hasan, is a thing that appears (yalūh) to the angels, so they read it. According to Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, it is made of white pearl; its length is the distance between the heaven and the earth, its width is the distance between the east and the west; its pen is light, and everything is inscribed in it. Muqatil said: it is to the right of the Throne. It was also said: its top is tied to the Throne, and its bottom is in the lap of a noble angel.
